title: Concurrent Detailed Routing with Pin Pattern Re-generation for Ultimate Pin Access Optimization
problem: Pin access has become a critical bottleneck in large-scale full-chip routing as feature sizes shrink and designs grow more complex. Conventional static pin patterns, predetermined during standard cell layout synthesis, occupy excessive routing resources and degrade overall routability.
motivation: Pin access optimization is essential for enabling successful full-chip routing and maintaining design quality in modern advanced-node chips.
method: The paper proposes concurrent detailed routing with dynamic pin pattern re-generation. It uses pseudopin extraction and routing techniques that guarantee at least one access point per I/O pin while releasing other predetermined access points for competing nets, thereby improving routing resource utilization and reducing conflicts.
key_novelty: First work to perform concurrent detailed routing with dynamic pin pattern re-generation to optimize pin accessibility instead of using static predetermined patterns.
contributions: Concurrent detailed routing methodology with pin pattern re-generation
Pseudopin extraction and routing technique for flexible pin access
89% resolution rate for previously unroutable local routing regions
Maintained power and timing performance without redesign overhead
